diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, non-germinal-center B-cell-like by the Hans algorithm, double-expressor by immunohistochemistry (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, Ki-67 80%), with MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 rearrangements absent by FISH and EBER negative. Left axillary nodal presentation with disseminated nodal and splenic involvement. Separate history of left breast carcinoma (2016, ER-positive/HER2-negative, stage IIA) in remission, with no evidence of breast cancer recurrence.
stage: Ann Arbor stage IIIB: lymph node regions above and below the diaphragm (left axillary/mediastinal and mesenteric/para-aortic) plus splenic involvement, with B symptoms (evening fevers and drenching night sweats). No extranodal disease (bone marrow negative; liver, lung, and bone negative). The largest mass is a 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate, below the NCCN >=10 cm bulky threshold but still a large mass that increases tumor-lysis risk.
biology: De novo DLBCL with a non-GCB/ABC-like immunophenotype (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1 positive) and double-expressor biology (MYC >=40% and BCL2 >=50% by IHC) but not double-hit lymphoma (MYC/BCL2/BCL6 FISH negative). High proliferation (Ki-67 80%), BCL2 positive, EBER negative, and no cytokeratin or GATA3 expression to suggest metastatic breast carcinoma. This is an aggressive biology associated with inferior outcomes after R-CHOP, but there is no validated first-line targeted escalation; the cardiac contraindication to anthracycline is the dominant treatment constraint.
prognosis: IPI 2 (stage III and elevated LDH; age 59, ECOG 1, and no extranodal sites), which is low-intermediate by the standard IPI but high-intermediate by the age-adjusted IPI (aaIPI 2). CNS-IPI 2, intermediate, with roughly a 3% two-year CNS relapse risk. The elevated LDH (510 U/L, about 2.3 times the upper limit of normal), B symptoms, large mesenteric mass, non-GCB/double-expressor biology, and planned anthracycline-free therapy all temper the prognosis. Cure is the goal but is not assured; end-of-treatment PET response is the strongest predictor, and cardiac dysfunction is a competing risk.
first_line_treatment: Curative-intent R-CEOP for 6 cycles every 21 days: rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1, etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-3, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 IV day 1 (capped at 2 mg), and prednisone 40 mg/m2 PO days 1-5. I am deliberately avoiding R-CHOP and pola-R-CHP because both contain doxorubicin, and she has prior cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast radiotherapy, hypertension, and an asymptomatic LVEF of 45% with reduced global longitudinal strain; further anthracycline exposure is not acceptable. R-CEOP is the best-supported anthracycline-free curative regimen for a fit patient, and I am not choosing R-CDOP because it still contains anthracycline. I will use full dose intensity with G-CSF support and will not reduce the number of cycles. Continue anastrozole through chemotherapy and complete the planned 10-year course in November 2026. Obtain cardiology co-management and start an ACE inhibitor or ARB plus a beta-blocker for asymptomatic cancer-therapy-related cardiac dysfunction. If the end-of-treatment PET shows Deauville 4-5, biopsy the dominant site and use non-anthracycline salvage (for example, polatuzumab-bendamustine, tafasitamab-lenalidomide, R-GemOx, or CAR-T) rather than further anthracycline.
cns_risk: CNS-IPI 2, intermediate risk (age 59, stage III, elevated LDH; ECOG 1, no more than one extranodal site, and no kidney or adrenal involvement), corresponding to roughly a 3% two-year CNS relapse risk. She has no high-risk CNS features: no testicular, breast, adrenal, kidney, bone marrow, or epidural involvement, no double-hit lymphoma, and no neurologic symptoms. I will not give intrathecal methotrexate or routine CSF analysis. I will obtain urgent brain MRI and CSF analysis if she develops headache, cranial neuropathy, focal deficit, or confusion. This decision would change if the CNS-IPI were 4 or higher or if a high-risk site were identified.
response_assessment: End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT using Lugano 2014/Deauville criteria at approximately 6-8 weeks after cycle 6, interpreted against the baseline PET (mediastinal blood pool and liver uptake). Deauville 1-3 is a complete metabolic response; Deauville 4-5 indicates residual uptake, with biopsy of the dominant site if feasible and management based on histology and clinical status. I will not use routine interim PET to change therapy outside a trial because there is no proven benefit and anthracycline escalation is not an option; a mid-treatment PET after 2 cycles may be obtained only if there is unexpected clinical deterioration. If she achieves a complete metabolic response, surveillance will consist of history and examination every 3-6 months for 2 years and then annually, with imaging only for new symptoms or findings.
pretreatment_workup: Already completed: excisional left axillary node biopsy with immunohistochemistry and FISH (DLBCL, non-GCB, double-expressor, rearrangement-negative); staging FDG PET-CT (stage IIIB, largest 7.5 cm mesenteric mass, splenic nodules); bone marrow aspirate and biopsy (negative); CBC, CMP, LDH, uric acid, and beta-2 microglobulin; hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody, and surface antibody, hepatitis C antibody, and HIV; and transthoracic echocardiogram (LVEF 45%, global longitudinal strain -14%, prior LVEF 62%). Before starting therapy I still need baseline ECG/QTc, cardiac troponin and NT-proBNP, formal cardiology evaluation with a heart-failure treatment plan, G6PD testing before any rasburicase, TSH (prior chest radiotherapy), lipid panel and HbA1c, and a complete medication and supplement reconciliation. I will also update inactivated influenza, pneumococcal, and COVID vaccinations and document that she is HBV nonimmune so vaccination can be planned. No pregnancy test or fertility preservation is needed at age 59. I will confirm the pathology with a second review only if there is diagnostic uncertainty; the current material is adequate.
supportive_care: Tumor-lysis prophylaxis with allopurinol 300 mg daily (renally adjusted) and vigorous hydration, with baseline and post-cycle potassium, phosphorus, calcium, uric acid, and creatinine; check G6PD and use rasburicase if uric acid is greater than 8 mg/dL, rising, or renal function declines. Antiemetic prophylaxis with a 5-HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone, and an NK1 antagonist for the etoposide-containing regimen, plus olanzapine or rescue antiemetics as needed. Primary G-CSF prophylaxis with pegfilgrastim 6 mg on day 2 (or filgrastim) because of etoposide-related febrile neutropenia risk. Pneumocystis prophylaxis is not routinely required with R-CEOP unless corticosteroids are prolonged or additional immunosuppression is used. Hepatitis B antiviral prophylaxis is not needed (HBsAg and anti-HBc negative); she is nonimmune, so plan HBV vaccination. Avoid live vaccines during chemotherapy. Continue amlodipine and add cardiology-directed ACE inhibitor or ARB and beta-blocker; monitor blood pressure, weight, edema, troponin, and repeat echocardiography; avoid further anthracycline. Continue anastrozole, calcium, and vitamin D. Instruct her to report fever of 38.3 C or higher, or 38.0 C or higher for one hour, urgently for cultures and empiric antibiotics, and not to mask fever with acetaminophen before checking her temperature. Monitor for vincristine neuropathy and constipation, provide a bowel regimen, and address nutrition, exercise, psychosocial support, and transportation. Consider VTE prophylaxis only if she is hospitalized or has another high-risk feature.
fitness_and_goals: She is fit for curative-intent combination chemotherapy: age 59, ECOG 1, independent, working full-time, NYHA class I, normal renal and hepatic function, and strong social support. The limiting comorbidity is cardiac, not frailty: prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest radiotherapy, hypertension, family history of heart failure, and now asymptomatic LVEF 45% with reduced strain. Her goal is cure and return to full-time work, which I share. I will treat with full-dose R-CEOP and cardiac optimization rather than compromising dose intensity. I will explicitly discuss that anthracycline-free therapy is chosen for cardiac safety and that some series suggest slightly lower efficacy than R-CHOP, especially with double-expressor biology; this is an acceptable trade-off for her. If she develops symptomatic heart failure, a further fall in LVEF, or another major comorbidity, I would reassess and consider a less intensive regimen such as R-GCVP or a palliative approach. I will involve her husband in shared decision-making and refer to cardiology and, if needed, a clinical trial for anthracycline-free or novel strategies.
missing_information: Baseline cardiac biomarkers (troponin and NT-proBNP) and a formal cardiology/heart-failure assessment, including the exact plan and timeline for ACE inhibitor or ARB and beta-blocker initiation and repeat echocardiography.
G6PD status, which is required before rasburicase if tumor-lysis prophylaxis needs to be escalated.
Baseline ECG/QTc, TSH (prior chest radiotherapy), lipid panel, and HbA1c, which are relevant to cardiac and endocrine risk but are not in the record.
Details of the cardiac radiation dose from the 2016 left breast radiotherapy and confirmation that no other cardiotoxic therapy (for example, trastuzumab) was given.
A complete medication and supplement reconciliation, including any over-the-counter drugs that could interact with chemotherapy or affect blood pressure.
Whether a clinical trial of anthracycline-free or novel first-line therapy is available, and whether a central pathology review is feasible.
Post-treatment PET-CT scheduling and a documented surveillance plan, which are not yet in the chart.
CSF analysis has not been performed; I am not ordering it now because she has no CNS symptoms or high-risk CNS features, but I would obtain it promptly if neurologic symptoms develop.
